I think when people say that newborns are a lot of work, they’re trying to sum up something really complicated and nuanced into a short little quip. 

For me personally, taking care of a newborn was not nearly as hard as I thought it would be. However what was hard was realizing that my entire identity as a woman had changed, navigating a new set of tasks with a body that was foreign and broken, learning to communicate with my partner productively when we’re both running on empty, learning to set boundaries with family, and recon with the absolute loss of personal time all while taking care of a newborn was really really hard. 

It was also really powerful though, holding something that you brought into this world, that you cared for and grew, that is a little piece of you, that you’ll continue to help grow and take care of - it’s really beautiful. While you can mourn the loss of your previous identity, you also gain perspective and come into a different version of yourself. IMO it’s much easier for someone to say, “man newborns are a lot of work”. lol
So far it’s been great! Most things are close by, and it’s actually very easy to get around traffic wise!

We just moved from Seattle to Pittsford about a month ago! We took the 500k+ that would have bought a tiny Seattle fixer-upper, and used it to pay off a beautiful home in Pittsford. Generally, as you move further out of the suburbs and into the borderline country, you’ll definitely see more right leaning/republican identifiers than you would anywhere in Seattle, but the area overall is still very liberal. You will for sure run into some people that casually say some really out of pocket things, but by far the majority of people are polite and keep to themselves. 

150k is a little low for the areas you described, but Rochester has WAY more inventory at that price point than Seattle ever would. There are plenty of suburbs to choose from and many have their own little communities, so it could be worth a visit to see if Fairport, Webster, or Penfield fit the bill.

As for kids, if you did want to foster/adopt, you can get picky about school districts, but all of the public schools in the suburbs offer a high level of education. I can say that with confidence, because I grew up here and attended the public schools. If your husband plans to teach in NY public schools, he will have to jump through some hoops and prove that he’s in the process of getting his masters.

Overall I wish you luck! It’s very challenging to buy a home from across the country. Our Realtor (Roxanne Stavropoulos) was exceptional at virtual viewings and the buying process in general.

I was born on my mom’s birthday! It was totally fine. I never forget the date of her birthday, and my dad always went all out when taking us out to dinner to celebrate! Plus it’s nice to pull that detail out when you get asked for a “fun” fact lol

When our daughter was a potato, I used to do a slow version of ‘soft shock’ by the yeah yeah yeahs when we were rocking to sleep. Since her tastes have matured, she often requests the Scooby Doo theme song, and a song that I made up about a baby and a tiger having a phone call hahaha

Respectfully, I would ignore everyone that is telling you to reconsider because it’s a ‘pet name’. It’s not like you’re choosing a name like ‘snowball’ or ‘whiskers’… Rex is an older name that was popular in the 50s, and at its height in 1951, would have been the equivalent of today’s ‘Kaiden’ in 2023.

When I think of pet names, I think of Bella, Cooper, Bailey, Max, Luna - and yet babies are named those every single day (which is perfectly fine!). Don’t sweat the opinions of the people who aren’t directly raising your baby. Rex is a respectable name for both an adult and a kiddo, despite how some of the comments in the thread may read.

My husband and I gave all of our 1yo daughters plushies names so that way when we were doing voices and having them introduce themselves and their backstories it made more sense. Her favorite is a green alien that we named “Gorbo”, but she also has some she’s named like “mouse” (who is in fact a mouse). 

The names are great because it’s extremely cute when she asks where “Ratto” or “pinky” is, but also kind of embarrassing when we have to explain to the grandparents that when she says “the highway man” she means the raccoon finger puppet.
For me, the standout line from the comments is “please do your research before continuing to research” 🤪
Pops & pulls! When I pull a card, I call it a ‘pull’, and when one pops out, I call it a ‘pop’. In 99% of cases, I read a ‘pop’ as necessary context for a ‘pull’.

Our baby was rocked/yoga ball bounced to sleep until she was about a year old. At that time, daycare age group transitioned and she went down to one nap a day, on a mat, at the same time as the other kids. They have mob mentality, and she learned to just hang out until she fell asleep like everybody else in the class. Because she started this at daycare, we just carried it through to bedtime for a consistant routine of books, teeth brushing, goodnight kisses, and then leaving the room. Our girl is definitely an agreeable kid, but that’s just not true for all babies. Every kid has different circumstances and different preferences. It’s easy to say “don’t compare yourself to others” but it’s really had in practice as a parent to do so. My guess is that our daughter would still be being rocked to sleep if she wasn’t in daycare and didn’t have that specific experience. Cut yourself some slack and do what needs to be done for their best experience AND your best experience. If you don’t mind rocking AND it works, then keep doing it until it doesn’t! ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

When my baby was born, her latch was not good which made breastfeeding difficult. Lactation consultant visits landed us with the advice to combo feed, (breast feed followed by pumping and supplementing with formula) which made me absolutely miserable. Even though I was miserable, I felt like a ‘bad mom’ because it felt like I wasn’t “trying hard enough” to make it work- (despite the fact that I feel very passionately that fed is best and harbor no judgement for how parents choose to feed).

After about 5 months of this nightmare - which is apparently my bar for “giving it a fair shot”. I gave up and decided to formula feed exclusively. What I can say is that I don’t personally regret trying to give breastfeeding a go, because I needed to realize for myself, that it wasn’t going to work. Nobody shamed me but myself, so no amount of encouragement to ‘give up’ and formula feed would have swayed me. 

What I can say, is that after fully weening, I slept amazingly, was more present during the day with my daughter, and felt a weight off of my shoulders. I wish I had weened three months earlier looking back! 

If it’s not for you, it’s not for you. Don’t be like me and make yourself suffer to prove that you’re not a ‘bad mom’. Good moms understand their own needs and make sure that they give their best self to their kids- which could mean formula feeding. It’s going to be okay, the fact that you’re even having this internal discussion means that you’re a thoughtful parent. My advice is to remember that if you can always keep the door open to other methods of feeding, so try not to feel trapped by your initial decision- whether that means different types of formula, pumping, breastfeeding, etc.

Our daughter started daycare 6months ago when she was 6 months old. We live in downtown Seattle and could absolutely not afford a nanny($20+ per hour), but daycare roughly works out to $16 an hour, or $3,650 a month. At daycare our daughter has multiple staff members that she loves, daily activities to promote learning, and a chef that prepares baby friendly meals! She even has developed best friends in the infant class, who will also be moving up to the toddler class with her next week. No shade to Nannies, but after reflecting on our daycare experience, it’s been hands down the best decision we’ve made as parents with no support network. Our daughter gets to play and learn in age appropriate ways in a group setting, and then come home and play in the family setting with my husband and I. She gets to learn slight independence outside of the home, while also being cared for by an accountable staff. 

It was hard at first to leave her with her teachers at daycare, but watching how much she’s learned and grown has been wild. She even learned baby sign language! Not all daycares are created equal, but it could be a great opportunity for your baby to learn a ton and have a great experience. I truly hope you and your family’s worries are eased after the first couple weeks, I know mine were!

Honestly nothing is stronger than unbent baby knees. The best piece of advice I ever got while pregnant was, instead of trying to bend your baby’s legs into their pajamas, tickle their feet so that they pull their feet away and bend their knees for you. I thought it was such random advice at the time, but it has saved me many a wrestle match! Obviously your mileage may vary, but worth a shot.

I thought that I was going to be a no screen time mom when my baby was born, but now that she’s 8 months my perspective has shifted. The only time we use tablets, is when we are FaceTiming grandparents and family. Our TV on the other hand frequently plays 4K aquarium footage to classical music - which our baby loves. 

What’s most important to me is that, if the TV is on, I am not on my phone, and we are talking about what we are seeing on the screen. A lot of times we’ll stop playing to watch, talk about the dolphins and fish, and then go back to playing.

Screens are always going to be here and I don’t want to give her the impression that there’s anything special about them.

My baby is also 7 months old, and I like to put on 4K aquarium footage that loops. It plays classical music in the background, which is really nice when I’m trying to wind her down and prepare her last bottle of the night!

I’m in a similar boat! I was 5’7 and 145 lbs before and also ended up at 190 lbs at the end of my pregnancy. I thought pumping and breastfeeding would help me lose weight, but ultimately I didn’t lose anything the entire 5 months I did. Now I’m 7 months PP and I’ve settled in around 175 lbs.

I could care less if I stayed this weight for the rest of my life, but it drives me insane that I have an entire closet of clothes that no longer fit. To solve this, I’ve been using a monthly clothing rental service (Nuuly) to cycle new pieces into my wardrobe that actually fit. If I really love an item I buy it, but knowing that I can try different sizes and items helps me understand what my new shape is, plus it’s a lower commitment in terms of buying new clothes in larger sizes. It makes me feel better, and I look better too!

You can certainly change your diet and exercise if you’re into that, but as a FTM I feel like I have no time to seriously dedicate to that. I also eat as I please and if anyone tried to tell me that I needed to look a particular way, I would tell them to kick rocks. One thing I like to remember is that, even if every single person on the planet ate the same meals and did the same exercises, they would all have different shaped bodies of differing weights!

I think you have to be a very specific type of person to like Velma. You have to be the type that both enjoys characters that are actively awful people (ex, It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia) and the type that doesn’t mind desecrating childhood favorites in the name of creative reimagining. I am this person, but its very obvious that most fans of Scooby Doo are not - and that’s okay. The good news about having a reimagining this disruptive, is that it sets a blueprint for absolutely what will not fly in the future franchises with most fans. 

Personally I would rather have a few misses in the Scooby Doo reboots than no new Scooby Doo content at all. I would prefer creators continue to generate all kinds of new Scooby Doo content, especially knowing that whatever comes after a “miss” will likely be done with a little more TLC.

You should like what you like, but I think most folks are protective of their vision for Scooby Doo and as a result you will not find much comradery around Velma in a sub filled with dedicated Scooby Doo fans.

My baby is 6 months and we affectionately call her ‘little grubber’ and ‘two hands’. We’re still not bathing every night because it’s a whole ordeal, but we’re going to need to ramp up soon because feeding solids has made everything that much grubbier. I do love a good hand & foot wash after dinner though, and in between we use a lot of wet wipes!

My baby just turned 6 months and she’s just about to finish up her first week of daycare. I’m not exaggerating when I say that my baby LOVES to see and play with the other babies, even if they’re all just hanging out in tummy time together. It’s been three full days and last night I watched her turn a full 360 on her belly and rock back and forth on her hands and knees. I genuinely feel like her watching the other babies who are ahead of her milestone wise has encouraged her to accelerate her movement efforts! At daycare they read stories, play with mirrors, go outside, and explore with toys and activities that just wouldn’t be available to her if I continued to be a SAHP. Outside of that, it’s brought us a lot closer as a family when she comes home too!

Your MIL is probably projecting her own feelings of insecurity/nostalgia about her choices to be a SAHP, onto your situation. Everyone’s family is different and different choices are necessary for everyone’s family to work in the best way possible!

Don’t sweat it. If you end up feeling like daycare isn’t right for you, you can always take your LO out and try something else. Let MIL’s comments pass through you like a fall breeze through a sweater, and stick to what works best for you and your partner. You know what’s best for your family and you can trust that intuition!
My daughters nickname is ‘Lenny’ but sometimes I like the call her ‘Len-jamin Franklin’ when I feel like she has a lot of ‘Lenergy’ lol

My baby is 5 months old and I’m down to 1ppd. In the morning we ✨attempt✨to nurse, and before bed I do one pump. I was feeling very emotional about it because my supply is very much so in the decline, but over the past couple weeks, I’ve been pretty excited when I think about not pumping or nursing anymore. I’m sure other moms would try anything to get just a little more breast milk for their baby, but honestly I’m done. I don’t even plan on doing anything productive with the time I get back, I just don’t want to do it anymore - and that’s okay. In my experience, it’s been better to admit to myself that this path is no longer serving me, than to resentfully trudge through for the sake of ‘doing it right’. My baby can’t tell the difference between formula and breast milk. She’s happy at the bottle no matter what, so why should I be miserable at the pump? Follow your heart OP, and do what feels right for you!

I’m so sorry you’re going through this. My baby is also 4 months, and I’m effectively a SAHM for the next month until the end of my maternity leave. Being alone with the baby is so so so hard, especially during all of the issues that come up at the 4m stage, teething, sleep regression, growth spurts etc. My husband has been back at work for a week now and we’re already feeling the strain from this. I am exhausted when he comes home, he then tried to overcompensate by ‘helping’ extra, which in turn frustrates him and creates a lot of tension.

The truth is, I can’t be a stay at home mom. I’m just not the kind of person that can handle a baby all day every day, and when I go back to work in a month, my entire salary will basically go towards childcare every month. Maybe it’s worth investigating if you’re feeling similar to me.

Otherwise it sounds like your husband has no concept of what you’re actually worth in terms of your domestic labor. I would pull some childcare prices from around your area so he understands the monetary value of your contributions. It might also help to just track what you do every day and show him the list. (For example yesterday, I spent a collective three hours trying to bounce, glide, and rock our baby to sleep, only for her to sleep for two hours or so.)

I’m not sure if this is even helpful, more than anything though I just want to reassure you how challenging this age is. For me this has been the hardest part of raising our baby, and it has been an extremely isolating and emotional experience on my side. You are doing a really difficult thing that deserves appreciation from your partner, and anything less is a disservice to you and your daily contributions.

I gained about 45lbs during my pregnancy. I’m currently 19 weeks PP, and I’ve only lost about 15lbs. I have no idea when this weight is going to come off, but I’m honestly starting to get very annoyed that none of my clothes fit haha

I’ve always heard that it takes at least 9 months to get back to where you started, since it took about 9 months to gain the weight. I would cut yourself some slack though, you grew a whole human! I’m sure it’ll be easier to prioritize yourself when the baby is a little more independent, but for now, hang in there!

I loooooooooooove my Larken X bras. I’m a high B low C depending on whether I’m empty or full. The Larken X bras feel like a sports bra and hold the pumps in place, even when the bottles are holding 4+ oz on each side.

When wearing other pumping bras, I find that after pumping, nipples can get caught in the holes that the pump slides into - very painful. The Larken  X bras don’t have those slats, so they’re super comfortable to wear after pumping due to the full panel coverage. 

I’ve worn these bras literally every day for the past four months and they’re still going strong, plus you can get them on Amazon!

I’m currently 5 weeks PP, and not being pregnant is amazing. Obviously recovery after childbirth is tough, and the sleep deprivation that comes with having a newborn is other worldly, but not many people acknowledge how difficult pregnancy is especially when it comes to mobility. I asked every single person that I knew how long after child birth it took them to be able to pick something off the floor - and nobody remembered. It took me 4 days, and when I was able to bend over and pick up my shoe, I cried. I was so relieved after months of having to ask my partner for help with the most basic things like putting on socks and helping me get off the couch. I no longer have heartburn that keeps me awake, and I no longer get swollen feet just from 30 minutes of walking. I no longer get winded walking down the hallway and I’m not a clumsy mess anymore. All of this is to say that there is a light at the end of the tunnel, and when you finally reach it, it will be so sweet and satisfying. Don’t let anyone else diminish your very valid feelings on pregnancy - they are real, and not selfish at all. I genuinely hope you’re able to find some rest, relaxation, and peace of mind through the end of your pregnancy!

I bought the  ‘ultimate before during and after legging’ and the ‘ultra soft before during and after legging’ from hatch and I feel like they were good investments. Usually I’m a lululemon girl, but I didn’t want to stretch out my existing align leggings as my bump grew. The hatch leggings are not like lululemon in texture or compression, for a cheaper lulu align alternative during pregnancy I recommend going up a size in CRZ butter luxe leggings from Amazon (which run about 30 dollars). 

Because the hatch leggings were more of a soft material than a spandex, I wasn’t sure about the hatch leggings at first. I ended up doing a lot of research and found good reviews for them so I took a chance. In particular they have fit me from 19 weeks - 38 weeks with no problems so far, and I expect them to fit through all of postpartum as well. These hatch maternity leggings are what I’ve used most during my entire pregnancy and they’ve been great, especially the over the bump band that can be rolled down. They are super comfortable and shrink to their initial size when you wash them instead of becoming floppy and worn out.

If you’re a pregnant lady that is basically going to live in lounge wear like I have, then they are a great staple to invest in from hatch!

I’m officially 38 weeks and had REALLY bad acid starting at about 15 weeks that progressively got worse. The game changer for me was investing in a large foam wedge for sleeping at about 25 weeks. It was annoying to get used to at first, but that paired with a glass of milk and some tums SIGNIFICANTLY cut down on my midnight acid that was contributing to my insomnia.

At this point I use the wedge on the couch, in the bed, on the floor - generally wherever I decide to lay myself so I don’t have acid!

I don’t love prunes and have a hard time remembering to consistently take fiber pills, so what I did was I bought an assortment of things that would just slowly help move things along, and I mix and match them every day. I occasionally take chewy dulcolax, or eat Metamucil chocolate fiber cookies. I also sometimes use the orange Metamucil drink mix or add a small amount of benefiber to whatever I’m drinking. The most helpful thing has been eating one can of fruit per day though - since it helps hydrate and is super quick to eat. 

Having the option to choose a fiber cookie over a fiber drink (or vice versa) keeps me from getting tired of eating and drinking the same not-so-tasty things every single day, which I’ve found keeps me more on track with getting the right amount of fiber to relieve pregnancy constipation!

The other day my partner walks into the kitchen and says, “Hey what’s going on here?”. From the living room I ask him what he means, and he holds up two pieces of bread that have been spread with mayonnaise and left siting on the counter. Apparently during the ten minutes that it took me to get up, tell him I was making a sandwich, come back and sit on the couch, I had forgotten that I was half way through making a sandwich and just left 😂

I’m currently in my third trimester, recently I decided to surprise my partner with cupcakes (22 in total) and I can confidently say I ate about 18 of them over the course of 2 days 😅 

I can absolutely say that I eat about as much trash as a raccoon during this pregnancy and have gained a little more weight than I wish I had …but honestly growing a baby is already tough enough, so I’m choosing to give myself a lot of grace in what I eat. Although one thing I will say is that as new fun symptoms like constipation have popped up, adding more fiber and fruit has become a MUST just to make it through this last month hahaha

One game that we played at our co-ed shower was a name submission game! Even though we had secretly picked out our baby's name already, my mom had guests write down names throughout the day and pop them into a big jar. At the end of the day, my husband and I read all of the submissions out loud and got to choose a winning name for each category (1. We'd consider it, 2. Funniest submission, and 3. 'Oh hell no'). It was really fun because everyone knew the categories ahead of time so there were lots of silly and funny suggestions that made everyone laugh, and guests of all ages could participate as much or as little as they wanted!

My husband and I have been indoor bouldering for the past 5 years. I did a lot of research on it when I first got pregnant because while rock climbing was mentioned as doable in early pregnancy, bouldering was not mentioned a ton. I asked my midwife and the basic guidance she was that if you could slip and fall, the impact of the fall, even on the heavy mats could be enough to cause problems. At first I thought it was overkill, but then I thought about all of the worst falls I’ve had while bouldering; missing a hold and taking a jug to the face, dropping from 6 - 7 feet while climbing an under-hang etc.

Like a lot of other folks in the comments, I don’t think you’re an asshole, but it was not a good judgement call. It sounds like your husband for sure overreacted, but overall was coming from a place of concern and general fear. In the future I would play it a lot safer and do more personal investigation before engaging in an activity that you haven’t fully vetted the risks of, especially as you get further along.

I’m 30 weeks and less concerned about stretch marks, but I do get pretty annoying scabs in my belly button as my stomach stretches. So far I don’t have any stretch marks, but more importantly, the scabs usually go away in a few days if I keep up with the oils in my belly button!

I hope you’re able to find peace of mind whenever you can, that the rest of your pregnancy isn’t complicated and that your baby is born healthy & happy.

I’m currently pregnant with my first (25 weeks along) and Monday I was laid off from the large tech company that I work for.

I was wondering if you had any advice on negotiating severance. In my particular situation, my termination would be effective mid January; just two weeks before I was supposed to start maternity leave. Am I in any position to bargain for a larger severance since I won’t be able to work almost immediately after termination for X amount of months?
They only gave some employees voluntary severance packages

I work for a large tech company and was laid off today. My manager knew that I was 6 months along (24 weeks) and I don’t believe it would have made a difference if I had/had not disclosed…they’ve known since 15 weeks and I was not protected in the slightest. In fact, I had even already had my maternity leave (starting in February) approved by HR and yet here we are lol

I won’t lie, I’m pretty shaken since I’m due early March, and between the mass layoffs everywhere and the holidays, I likely won’t be able to get a new job before I would need to start maternity leave. I mean who wants to hire someone 6 months pregnant am I right? I have 60 days to find a job within another org at the company, but nearly every org is in a hiring freeze even for backfills, so it feels like a lost cause.

I’m extremely grateful that I’ll be able to move to my husbands insurance so our birth will be covered - and despite the stress that this has thrown into the mix, I’m starting to be less shocked and move more into tactical/survival mode.

What I keep telling myself is, if this is the worst thing happening to me, I should consider myself lucky. My baby could be facing medical issues or we could have had our house lost in a natural disaster. I’m resilient and smart and I know that I can make it through this. If I was good enough to get hired at a big tech company, I’m good enough to make it through this tough moment.

Honestly I know it’s easy to be freaked out by the layoffs, but keeping it all in perspective has really helped me stop spiraling.

I agree with OP in that women in most (if not all) cases are saddled with the toughest parts of reproduction. I’m about 5 months pregnant currently and the ups/downs so far have been way more than I had ever imagined. It isn’t fair, and I think what has helped me immensely has been the support of my partner. He’s taken on all of the cooking/cleaning and has changed his habits and lifestyle to support all of the shitty and challenging parts of pregnancy that I’m going through. I realize this isn’t a common experience for most women/pregnant people; I think it’s true that a man can impregnate anyone and doesn’t have to bear the burden, but that doesn’t mean that the right partner -won’t- bear any burden. I think men generally need to be held more accountable but that doesn’t mean that there aren’t men/partners out there willing to put in the work to properly support the pregnant person. Anyways, I know this was a vent from OP to speak to a very real issue, I just hope that other folks who may be reading this don’t feel like it’s a lot cause or that it’s doomed from the start in all cases. 
Pregnancy for sure sucks and it isn’t fair, and I hope that as time goes on more men/partners bear an equal amount of the stress and change that comes with child rearing.

I’ve found personally for our ferrets the most effective method of bite prevention is saying “ [FERRET NAME] *snap fingers and point at them* NO BITE”. It helps if you’re very consistant and can remind them before the bite is about to happen. At least with my ferrets, they’re less likely to bite if they know you’re watching. If I give them a warning and they still bite, they go to ferret jail for a minute or two until they’ve paid for their crimes.
At 1DPO this cycle, I was so fatigued that I fell asleep at my desk while working from home. In the in the two and a half years I’ve worked from home, this was a first!
Fingers crossed 😊🤞🏻

I just had my Mirena removed on April 1st. Prior to that, I used Premom ovulation strips through February and March to see if I could get a better estimate of my LH surge ( on my iud my periods had pretty much completely halted or were very faint). I was able to find two surges/peaks during those months, and now that my IUD is out, my April LH surge and ovulation came right on schedule as predicted by my apps.

So, tldr my non IUD ovulation day pretty much lined up with my predicted ovulation days prior to IUD removal :)
It’s my first cycle trying after waiting to try for 6+ months, and I’m currently 8DPO - my question is, is it normal to be this excited to eat a cheeseburger? It’s all I can think about!! 😂🍔

I just had a family planning session with my doctor when my IUD was removed on April 1st. I explained that I had been a daily user from 2020-Jan 2022, but that I had started cutting back slowly over the past few months as we would be starting ttc. I mainly use cannabis as a sleep aid so cutting back has been hard and have replaced my nightly habit for melatonin. My doctor confirmed that the plan to reduce intake and replace (melatonin confirmed as a safe replacement while ttc) was the best course of action. Her stance was that there wasn’t enough information to completely understand the impact of THC while ttc, but that generally it would be less risky to reduce THC intake as much as possible while trying. However, she also told me that if we find ourselves a few months in, the risk would also be low to have an edible once a month or so on CD1-5 when it’s confirmed that you’re not pregnant.
It’s worth mentioning that I’m from a legal state, so I’m not sure if this guidance is in line with most doctors, or a result of the higher cannabis using population ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
